Consider a directed weighted graph G(V, E), where V is the set of vertices and E is the set of edges. Suppose we use adjacency list to implement the graph. Consider a sequence of |V| operations with each corresponding to a different vertex in V. For the operation for vertex v, the cost is assumed to be the number of outgoing edges from v.  (a) What is the cost of the worst possible single operation in this sequence of operations? (b) What is the average amortized cost of the above sequence of operations based on aggregate analysis?

message.content:
The cost of the worst possible single operation is |V| - 1, which occurs when a vertex has outgoing edges to every other vertex in the graph. The total cost of the entire sequence of |V| operations equals the sum of all out-degrees, which is exactly |E| (the total number of edges).

* **Part (a):** The worst-case cost of a single operation is |V| - 1, since a vertex can have at most |V| - 1 outgoing edges in a directed graph (one to each other vertex).

* **Part (b):** Using aggregate analysis, the amortized cost per operation is |E| / |V|, because the total cost across all |V| operations is |E| (the sum of out-degrees of all vertices), and dividing by the number of operations |V| gives the average amortized cost.

(a) Worst possible single operation:
The cost of the operation for vertex v is the number of outgoing edges from v, i.e., the out-degree of v. The worst case would be when a single vertex has the maximum possible number of outgoing edges. In a directed graph with |V| vertices, the maximum number of outgoing edges from a single vertex is |V| - 1 (edges to all other vertices). So the worst possible single operation has cost |V| - 1.

(b) Average amortized cost using aggregate analysis:
The total cost of all |V| operations is the sum of the out-degrees of all vertices, which equals |E| (the total number of edges in the graph).

The amortized cost per operation is the total cost divided by the number of operations:
Amortized cost = |E| / |V|

This is the average amortized cost based on aggregate analysis.
